Electric Dreams is the canonical works record for PKD's short-story collection. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is Electric Dreams (Unknown). The archive copy runs 180 pages.

structure.form: ten-story anthology, each story preceded by a screenwriter/producer introduction

motifs: Suburban and domestic reality's instability under technological or bureaucratic pressure
Cold War-era paranoia and loyalty anxiety
The question of authentic humanity under conditions of automation or surveillance
reading.significance: As a screen-adaptation tie-in volume, Electric Dreams functions as both a companion to the television series and an accessible entry point into Dick's short fiction, and its paired introductions -- each screenwriter reflecting on adapting a specific story -- offer a useful secondary-source window into how contemporary television writers read and reworked Dick's mid-century concerns for a 2010s audience. Each of the ten stories collected here has its own dedicated close-reading dossier elsewhere in this corpus (autofac, the-commuter, the-hanging-stranger, the-hood-maker, foster-you-re-dead, human-is, the-father-thing, the-impossible-planet, exhibit-piece, sales-pitch).
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the anthology as a publishing and adaptation artifact; readers seeking analysis of the individual stories should consult each story's own dossier.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.

critical_caution: This is a tie-in anthology reprinting ten previously published Dick stories, each of which already has its own dedicated close-reading dossier in this corpus; this entry describes the collection as a publishing object rather than re-reading its contents.
